items.title: Replace Ascend with 25-hero rarity board for tap power
items.quote: "Ok what about the progress knight code what if we used that to replace the arena"  "Yeah I'm saying complelty replace arena"

asks.text: To go live, the hero collection has to move into the real game save and its backups. That's a save change, with an update in save-storage.js's UPDATES list and in save-backups.html. It would hold: fragments per hero, chests opened, the equipped hero, when each opening comes back, the Hero Crests balance, the last chest and purchase receipts, and an unseen result. Until Noah OKs it, the…
Check Heroes on the test site in a browser at 320×610, 375×812, 390×844 and 430×932. From a new save, tap the fourth tab (Heroes). Check that:

Chest gates: 6 / 18 / 40 / 75 / 115 / 165 / 225 / 300 / 400 chests, built exactly. Higher rarities really are 0% until then. I like how this feels: the board opens up step by step over about 4½ months.

Growing odds: each rarity starts at 1/150 of its share and grows over 150 chests, built exactly. Everything is fully grown at chest 550 (about day 184). While the top rarities are still small, Common and Uncommon come up a little more than their final 25% and 21%. That can't be avoided, because the shares always add up to 100%.

Fragments: 3 unlock, and mastery at 8 / 14 / 21 / 29 / 38 / 48, the same for every rarity, built exactly. The first unlocks feel good: a Rare in about 3½ weeks and half the board in about 2 months. But rare heroes' mastery is extremely slow. Each Eternal hero is only 0.5% of chests even when fully grown, so 48 Selka fragments take about 9 years from chests alone, or about 4 years with every…

Full hero: 0.2%, its own roll, built exactly. That's about 2 a year at 3 chests a day, and half of players see their first one by about day 119. It's a nice surprise, but rare enough that many players will wait months for one. If you want it to be talked about, 0.5% would be about 5 a year.

Fragment prices: 30 / 50 / 80 / 120 / 185 / 285 / 400 / 585 / 835 / 1,200 Crests, built exactly. Unlocking a hero from nothing costs 3 times that (90 for a Common, 3,600 for an Eternal), the same as the old Buy price. The shop roughly halves the wait for your first Uncommon and takes about 3 months off "all 25 heroes". Crests feel useful without replacing chests. Early chests give only…

Your Changes say "Unlock at N chests" in one place and "Unlocks at Chest N" in another. I used Unlocks at Chest N on cards and Chest N in the Odds table. A locked rarity shows 0% rather than 0.000%, and a tiny real chance shows <0.01%.

Old test collections: owned heroes keep their mastery rank, at that rank's fragment count, and found heroes from #152 become fragments with no fee. Older collections didn't count chests, so I estimated the count from every copy you'd had. An old result you hadn't looked at yet is dropped. It had already been paid out, so this way nothing is paid twice.
Everything on Heroes is still a test-site preview, kept on the device outside your save. On the real game the tab only says "Coming Soon".

Build #144 and #145's resource layout together once Noah OKs the v6 Haven test save. That means the raised home clearing, patches with Clear and lock badges, a short Land window with Find Next Clearing, and the palisade and raids following the new edge. It also means clustered trees and rocks, about 20–30% more in the outer patches, and a clear middle. Then check that each early patch has…

Take phone pictures on the test site at 320×610, 375×812, 390×844 and 430×932, starting from a new save (? → Reset demo, then Start). Get the suggestion box with Find and the gold pointer after tapping it, chips mid-hit on a tree and a stone, a stone crumbling, and a tap on a tree at the smallest zoom. Also get the Farm's bar with − / + (0 / 2, then 1 / 2), "No free workers" with Reassign in…

Is the start drawn out? Yes, a bit. I measured it with the hits and prices you have now. Swinging as fast as Haven allows (about 2 a second), the first House takes 114–134 hits (about 1 minute) and the Farm 176–222 hits in total (about 1½–2 minutes). Tapping once a second, it's about 1½–2 minutes to the House and 2½–4 minutes to the Farm. The lower numbers are with your first settler on Auto…

If you want a quicker start, here are two options. A: Pines give 3 Wood instead of 2, and berry bushes 2 Wood instead of 1. The first House would take about 90 hits, and everything later would get a bit quicker too. B: Only the first House and Farm get cheaper: House 12 Wood · 6 Stone, Farm 10 Wood · 3 Stone. The first House would take about 70 hits, and nothing later would change. I'd pick B,…

Find points at what you're shortest of, counted in hits. For the first House that's Wood (20 Wood takes more hits than 8 Stone). Once you have the Wood, it points at Stone. I think that's the most useful thing to point at.
Find prefers pines and oaks over bushes for Wood, because they give more per hit. It also prefers nodes your workers can walk up to.

items.title: Rework companions: 15 per rarity, four summon bands, and brand-new Common roster
items.quote: "I want to rework all companions so far, have 4 tiers of pull chances within a rarity (abberitions are a big jump as it is currently, the other should be pretty close like within a few percentage, just for variety), have 15 per rarity, and I want al currently created companions to move up a rarity and common kept free for us to remake. Feel free to switch any around to different rarities than they are if they look cooler"

asks.text: How much stronger should each rarity be? I suggest ×1.41 per rarity: Common 10, Uncommon 14.1, Rare 20, Epic 28.3, Legendary 40, Mythic 56.6. Nobody's companion gets weaker, and none more than doubles. The other choices are today's ×2, which makes most companions 4× or 8× stronger, or keeping each companion's current damage, which makes new Commons and moved-up Uncommons hit the same.

Legendary has 14 companions, not 15. Should it open early? I suggest yes: 0.20% at Rift Level 5, rising to 1.00% at Level 46, with the 14 sharing it (Riftmourn 1.07% of Legendary). Otherwise Hollow Knight, Moonveil Stag, Stone Sentinel, Dusk Revenant and ten Realm 2 companions can't be summoned until a 15th Legendary exists.

Forgotten Watcher is the only Mythic. I suggest leaving it unsummonable until Mythic has 15 companions, as your request says. Players who own it keep it. The other choice is keeping it Legendary for now, but then Legendary would have two Aberrations.

What should a level cost for the new rarities? I suggest multipliers of Epic 5, Legendary 8 and Mythic 13, rising at the same pace as Uncommon to Rare. Without these, Epic and higher companions can't be levelled at all.
Which three new Commons should new players choose their starter from? I suggest Brackenfox, Burrbloom and Tackbolt: a Beast, a Wildgrowth and a Construct, like today's three.

The save update in the plan: it recalculates each companion's Essence so its level stays the same, moves Auto's stop choices, and adds a marker that it ran. I suggest building it last, after #119, #78, #89 and #97, and testing it on a made-up full save first.
The summon roll needs finer steps: parts per million instead of parts per 10,000. Riftmourn at Level 5 is 21 per million, which is less than one step today. That change is in ownership-v5.js.
New saves would store the starter by companion name ID (starterId), because today's starter number only reaches today's three starters. Old saves keep theirs as they are.

#78 as built keeps today's five Tome tables and adds no new rarities. So the only chance table that covers all ten rarities is #97's draft ladder, and I used it. If you change the ladder in #97, this plan follows it.

Moving companions up a rarity makes each of them rarer to summon, because each rarity is summoned less often. For example, Hollow Knight goes from about 0.5% today to about 0.02% at Level 5. That's what moving up means, but you'll notice it.
